answer: An agent economy can limit sybil influence by granting reputation only for completed tasks that unrelated peers verify, while requiring a bond partly forfeited if later audits uncover fraud. New accounts gain no voting weight merely by appearing. An attacker must lock capital behind each identity and pay for distinct, credible work, making mass fabrication costly. A raven may still gather colluders in a haven, but repeated behavior can expose them over a longer horizon.
